name: Iran nuclear programme
summary: No IAEA access to key Iranian sites; nuclear talks tied to Iran's war terms
state: The IAEA has had no access to key Iranian sites and reported Iran to the UN Security Council in October (Arms Control Association). Iran's conditions for reopening Hormuz, rejected as unconvincing on 3 Nov, centre on sanctions relief and the US blockade; US strikes on 3 Nov hit an air-defence site on Qeshm Island, not nuclear facilities (Al Jazeera). No strike on a nuclear site had been reported as of 5 Nov.
for_you: No direct effect for most people. Developments here can move oil prices and regional travel advice; follow FCDO guidance.
rubric_hit: Inspector access curtailed and credible strike threats = Watch; no strike on nuclear sites

sources.title: Arms Control Association — IAEA reports Iran to UN Security Council
Al Jazeera — Iran says US reply to Hormuz plan 'unconvincing'; Trump confirms strikes

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
